content.value_statement: Complex code becomes hard to change and risky to extend. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through focused refactoring with tests and reviewable steps.
actual_capabilities: Identifies code smells, risky dependencies, and maintainability hotspots.
Creates incremental refactor plans with clear order and impact.
Applies clean code and SOLID patterns to improve structure.
Keeps external behavior stable unless the user approves changes.
Adds or updates tests and reports verification results.
Uses the included playbook for examples and decision frameworks.
limitations: Not intended for one-line fixes or documentation-only requests.
Needs source code and expected behavior to verify safe changes.
Cannot guarantee behavior preservation without tests or review.
Large legacy systems may require several focused refactoring passes.

use_cases.title: Untangle Legacy Modules
use_cases.description: Break large methods and mixed responsibilities into smaller, testable units while preserving current behavior.

use_cases.title: Prepare Code for Features
use_cases.description: Reshape brittle code before adding new requirements, so future changes are easier to review and maintain.

use_cases.title: Improve Review Quality
use_cases.description: Get a structured refactor plan, expected impact, and verification notes before merging broad cleanup work.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Refactor Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a small module.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this module for code smells. Suggest a small refactor plan, then apply the safest first change and explain how to verify it.

prompt_templates.title: Reduce Duplication
prompt_templates.prompt: Find duplicated logic in these files. Refactor it into shared helpers only where it improves clarity, then update related tests.

prompt_templates.title: Apply SOLID Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this service for SOLID violations and tight coupling. Propose incremental changes, then implement the highest-value slice with tests.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Safe Migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a larger legacy area.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a staged refactor plan for this legacy component. Preserve public behavior, identify risks, add characterization tests, and implement stage one.

output_examples.input: A long order-processing class mixes validation, persistence, notifications, and logging.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a prioritized refactor plan, separates responsibilities, and lists tests that confirm order behavior remains unchanged.

output_examples.input: Several controllers repeat the same input checks and error handling.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies shared validation rules, proposes a small abstraction, and reports which tests were added or updated.

output_examples.input: A service depends directly on database and email implementations.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends dependency inversion, introduces interfaces where useful, and explains the review impact of each change.

best_practices: Start with tests or characterization checks before changing structure.
Keep each refactor small enough for focused review.
Verify behavior after each slice and document remaining risks.
anti_patterns: Do not combine refactoring with unrelated feature changes.
Do not introduce abstractions without a clear maintenance benefit.
Do not rewrite working code when a smaller structural change is enough.

faq.question: Can this skill change production behavior?
faq.answer: It is designed to preserve behavior unless the user explicitly approves a behavior change.

faq.question: Does it write tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks the agent to update tests and include verification notes when code changes are made.

faq.question: Is it useful for small fixes?
faq.answer: It is best for refactoring work. A one-line bug fix usually does not need this skill.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it include language-specific examples?
faq.answer: Yes. The playbook includes examples across common languages and refactoring patterns.

faq.question: How should I provide context?
faq.answer: Provide the target files, current behavior, test commands, and constraints before asking for changes.
